title: Querying Counterfactuals on Tissue Graphs with Supervised Disentanglement
abstract: arXiv:2606.08493v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Tissue graph counterfactuals ask what a cell would express if its spatial neighborhood were altered, a question central to predicting cell behavior in tissues. Existing methods, however, present only specific instances of such queries. In this work, we first formalize tissue graph counterfactuals as a class of spatial interventions that either rewire connections between cells (edge perturbation) or modify the expression of their neighbors (node perturbation). We then introduce Cellina, a framework that uses supervised disentanglement to decompose a cell's intrinsic state from its spatial context, using the latter as a conditioning input for in-silico perturbation predictions. Across benchmarks spanning over 2.5 million spatially-resolved cells in observational and interventional screens, Cellina outperforms both spatially-informed and non-spatial competitors in in-silico perturbations, while training as fast as non-spatial meth

translated_title: 基于监督解耦的组织图反事实查询
translated_abstract: 组织图反事实旨在回答这样一个问题：如果一个细胞的空间邻域发生改变，它会表达什么？这是预测组织中细胞行为的核心问题。然而，现有方法只能呈现此类查询的特定实例。在这项工作中，我们首先将组织图反事实形式化为一类空间干预，这些干预要么重新连接细胞之间的连接（边扰动），要么修改其邻居的表达（节点扰动）。随后，我们提出了Cellina框架，该框架利用监督解耦将细胞的内在状态从其空间环境中分解出来，并将空间环境作为计算机内扰动预测的条件输入。在涵盖超过250万个具有空间分辨率的观察性与干预性筛选细胞的基准测试中，Cellina在计算机内扰动预测方面优于空间感知和非空间的竞争方法，同时训练速度与非空间方法相当。
tldr: 该论文提出Cellina框架，通过监督解耦将细胞的内在状态与空间上下文分离，并首次将组织图反事实形式化为边扰动和节点扰动两类空间干预，在覆盖超过250万个细胞的基准测试中超越了现有空间与非空间方法。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Cellina, a framework that uses supervised disentanglement to decompose a cell's intrinsic state from its spatial context, and formalizes tissue graph counterfactuals as edge and node perturbation spatial interventions, outperforming both spatially-informed and non-spatial competitors on benchmarks spanning over 2.5 million cells.
